record.context_brief: Cardinal symmetry numbers of the free group F2
record.original_question: For the free group F_2 on two generators, is the cardinal symmetry number MS_r^+(F_2) uncountable for every finite number of colors r?

evidence.quote: Theorem 8.15 implies that the free group F2 with two generators has uncountable cardinal symmetry number MS+2 (F2), which means that for each 2-coloring of F2 there is an infinite monochromatic symmetric subset of F2.
Problem 8.18. Is MS+r(F2) uncountable for any finite cardinal r?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $F_2$ denote the free group on two generators. For a group $G$, a subset $S \subseteq G$ is called symmetric if there exists $g \in G$ such that $S = gS^{-1}g$, i.e., $S$ is invariant under the involution $x \mapsto gx^{-1}g$ for some $g \in G$. Given a positive integer $r$, an $r$-coloring of $G$ is a function $\chi : G \to \{1,\dots,r\}$. Define
$$MS_r^+(G) = \min_{\chi : G \to \{1,\dots,r\}} \sup\{|S| : S \subseteq G \text{ is symmetric and monochromatic under } \chi\},$$
where the supremum is taken over all symmetric subsets of $G$ that are monochromatic with respect to $\chi$, and the minimum is taken over all $r$-colorings of $G$. The quantity $MS_r^+(G)$ is called the cardinal symmetry number of $G$ with $r$ colors.

Question: Is $MS_r^+(F_2)$ uncountable for every finite cardinal $r \geq 1$?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches surface foundational work by Banakh, Verbitsky, Vorobets, and Protasov on monochromatic symmetric subsets in colored groups, but no source explicitly resolves the question of whether $MS_r^+(F_2)$ is uncountable for all finite $r$. The case $r=2$ is known to give an uncountable value, but no resolution for general $r$ was located.

status_evidence.title: A Ramsey Treatment of Symmetry
status_evidence.snippet: Foundational paper introducing cardinal symmetry numbers and monochromatic symmetric subsets in colorings of groups.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the framework for $MS_r^+$ but does not resolve the free-group case for general $r$.

status_evidence.title: Monochrome symmetric subsets of colored groups
status_evidence.snippet: Studies infinite monochrome symmetric subsets in colorings of arbitrary groups.
status_evidence.claim: Provides results on infinite groups but does not specifically settle $MS_r^+(F_2)$ for all finite $r$.
